screenSummary.playArea: The play area shows a 20-metre accelerator track with three lanes: a light pulse, the particle as Newton predicts it, and the particle as relativity predicts it. All three start together. Below are two charts: speed (or momentum) against time, and speed squared against kinetic energy, with Bertozzi's 1964 measurements on electrons.
screenSummary.controlArea: Choose an electron or a proton, set the accelerating field, choose what the left chart plots, and show or hide Bertozzi's data. A button jumps to the chapter's worked example, an electron accelerated through 2 megavolts. Play, pause, step and restart the run with the time controls.
screenSummary.interactionHint: Press Play and watch the Newtonian particle overtake the light pulse while the real particle never does.

accelerate.currentDetailsPattern: At {{time}}, the {{particle}} has travelled {{distance}} with kinetic energy {{kinetic}} and speed {{speed}}. Newton would give it speed {{newtonSpeed}}.
accelerate.currentDetailsAtStart: The {{particle}} is at rest at the start of the track. Press Play to accelerate it.

controls.fieldHelp: Strength of the accelerating field in megavolts per metre; the force on the particle is its charge times this field.
controls.chartQuantityHelp: Plot speed or momentum against time.
controls.workedExampleHelp: Jumps to the moment an electron has been accelerated through 2.00 megavolts, so its kinetic energy is 2.00 MeV.
controls.restartHelp: Returns the particle to the start of the track.

screenSummary.playArea: The play area shows a right triangle whose legs are the momentum pc and the rest energy mc² and whose hypotenuse is the total energy E, a bar splitting the total energy into rest energy and kinetic energy, and a graph of energy against momentum with the particle's mass shell and the light line E = pc. A table lists speed, Lorentz factor, momentum, kinetic energy, total energy and invariant mass in the lab and for a moving observer.
screenSummary.controlArea: Choose a particle, choose which quantity to set (speed, momentum, kinetic energy or total energy), and set it with the slider. A second slider sets the speed of an observer moving along the particle's direction.
screenSummary.interactionHint: Push the speed slider towards its maximum and watch the momentum and energy grow without limit.

energyMomentum.currentDetailsPattern: {{particle}} with momentum {{momentum}}, kinetic energy {{kinetic}}, total energy {{energy}}, moving at {{speed}}. Invariant mass {{mass}}.
energyMomentum.frameDetailsPattern: An observer moving at {{frameSpeed}} measures total energy {{energy}} and momentum {{momentum}}; the invariant mass is the same.

controls.particleHelp: Choose the particle whose energy and momentum are shown.
controls.customMassHelp: Rest energy of the custom particle, in MeV.
controls.setQuantityHelp: Choose which quantity the slider below controls; the others follow.
controls.quantitySliderHelp: Sets the particle's motion through the chosen quantity.
controls.observerSpeedHelp: Speed of an observer moving along the particle's direction, as a fraction of c. Positive means moving the same way as the particle.
